messages:
Katie Lee: Heads up — last night's tensor-export batch hit gpunode-7 and we had repeated job failures. Observed huge local NVMe IOPS spikes (~350k r/s) and the ephemeral cleaner kicked in, apparently racing with checkpoint writes. Putting logs here.

Raj Patel: saw that too. dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0n1: queue full, io_wait 120ms
[ 1234.568100] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 0
[ 1234.568200] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
```

Tomas Müller: likely IO saturation -> high scheduler latency -> cleaner starts removing old ephemeral dirs to free inodes and space. If cleaner tries to rm while process is fsync'ing a checkpoint you can get corruption or failed writes. Also saw transient ENOENT in application logs.

Katie Lee: repro steps we used:
```
fio --name=burst --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=128 --numjobs=12 --runtime=600 --size=10G --group_reporting
# or run 24 export workers with batch_size=4096
```
Output shows latencies spiking >500ms for many ops.

ops-sre: adding observed meta — this only repros on nodes with 2x1.6TB local NVMe (nvme firmware a1.2) during concurrent model export + continuous evals. Suspect cleaner threshold is too eager and eviction lock isn't held across writer path.

Raj Patel: temp mitigation we pushed earlier:
- throttle export workers from 24 -> 8
- add a 10s jitter to ephemeral-cleaner loop
- pin heavy jobs to dedicated-gpu-large pool in us-west-2 where local storage is 3.2TB and IOPS headroom is higher

Tomas Müller: longer-term fixes to consider:
- hold a per-path RW lock in cleaner so rm doesn't collide with fsync path
- adjust cleaner reclaim_threshold from 0.55 -> 0.75 (less aggressive)
- limit per-container blkio (cgroups v1: blkio.throttle.write_bps_device) or use cgroup v2 io.max to cap IOPS for heavy jobs
- push NVMe firmware that improves queue handling

Katie Lee: also saw race where cleaner removed the checkpoint parent dir before process finished creating atomic symlink -> app saw ENOENT and retried, then failed after N retries. Adding an atomic rename+flock will help.

infra-bot: reminder — rolling kernel for the last firmware patch is scheduled Tue 03:00 UTC. Will need maintenance window if we want to roll NVMe firmware.

ops-sre: immediate action items:
- (Katie) reduce nightly export parallelism to 6 for 48h — DONE
- (Raj) land cleaner lock PR with a short backoff and non-blocking check — WIP
- (Tomas) evaluate cgroup v2 io.max per job and give recommended caps
- (infra-bot) schedule node drain for firmware roll (if agreed)

Katie Lee: thanks. If anyone sees the corruption again ping here with node and job id. Prefer to keep heavy repro on staging-dense for a bit to avoid customer impact. :thumbsup:
